title: Claude Discovers Truly Subquadratic 3SUM & Subcubic APSP Algorithms (Lean 4)
aiSystem: Internal Anthropic Claude Model (16M-token autonomous search + Lean 4)
whyItMatters: Autonomously refutes two foundational pillars of fine-grained complexity—discovering deterministic O(n^1.9992) 3SUM and O(n^2.9995) APSP algorithms certified in Lean 4 and vetted by Alman & Vassilevska Williams.
summary: In a landmark arXiv paper co-authored with Columbia’s Josh Alman and MIT’s Virginia Vassilevska Williams, Anthropic’s internal research model of Claude autonomously discovered—during a 16-million-token search—deterministic truly subquadratic O(n^1.9992) algorithms for 3SUM and truly subcubic O(n^2.9995) algorithms for All-Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP) on polynomial-weight integer graphs via triangles in sparse lopsided graphs. The result simultaneously refutes the 1995 3SUM hypothesis (31 years open), the 1962 Floyd–Warshall cubic APSP barrier (~64 years), Exact Triangle, and Zero-Weight k-Clique, with the core proof certified in Lean 4 with Mathlib and independently checked, simplified, and extended by Alman and Vassilevska Williams.
technicalHighlights: Achieves deterministic O(n^1.9992) time for 3SUM and O(n^2.9995) time for integer-weighted APSP, breaking both the quadratic 3SUM and cubic APSP barriers simultaneously.
Also refutes the Exact Triangle and Zero-Weight k-Clique hypotheses via a new reduction through sparse lopsided triangle detection.

Discovered autonomously by Claude in a 16M-token session, machine-certified in Lean 4 with Mathlib, and verified, simplified, and extended by leading fine-grained complexity theorists Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams.
caveats: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (v1) whose asymptotic exponents (1.9992 and 2.9995) carry large constant factors and apply to polynomial-weight integer inputs rather than arbitrary real-RAM weights; conference/journal peer review is ongoing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Refutes two of the three central hardness pillars of fine-grained complexity theory (3SUM since 1995 and APSP since 1962) in one stroke.
scoreRationale.ripple: Forces a sweeping reassessment of hundreds of conditional lower bounds across computational geometry, stringology, dynamic graphs, and data structures.
scoreRationale.verification: Both machine-certified in Lean 4 with Mathlib and thoroughly vetted, simplified, and co-authored by two of fine-grained complexity’s foremost authorities.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomously uncovered by Claude in a single 16M-token search after decades of human attempts yielded only polylogarithmic improvements.
